Hi Julia — great to hear from you. High level answers up front, followed by an acceptance-test proposal below.

TL;DR:
- We commit to a baseline tokens/sec (T) per GPU pool size in the term sheet. For your target profile (mix of chat generation + shorter completions) we estimate 9.5k tokens/sec steady with bursts to 27k tokens/sec for a 4-GPU pool (A100 equivalent).
- Latency target: p50 < 80ms token-gen, p95 token-gen < 220ms under agreed steady-state throughput.
- Credits: standard: 5% monthly service credit if monthly availability/throughput falls below 98% of committed tokens/sec; escalated: 10% if below 95%. We are open to revising bands for enterprise commits.

Proposed measurement & acceptance plan (summary):
1) Define workload profile: 70% chat-style (avg 64 tokens/output), 30% batch completions (avg 256 tokens). Use your representative prompt set (you mentioned clinical summarization) — please provide 50 representative prompts.
2) Run a 72-hour acceptance window during onboarding:
   - First 24h: dry run + profiling (no SLA enforcement).
   - Next 48h: two 24h measurement windows to compute steady-state tokens/sec and latency percentiles.
   - Use continuous load generation clients from two geographic regions (us-west/us-east) to validate egress routing.
3) Measurement hooks: server-side token counters, per-request latency histograms, and KV-cache hit-rate logs. All metrics exported to a shared read-only dashboard for the customer.
4) Test harness & artifacts: we will provide a measurement-playbook (PDF) and a spreadsheet with threshold buckets. Marcus will attach the detailed matrix.

Attachments: throughput-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (proposed), measurement-playbook.pdf (detailed steps).

Next steps: If this matches your needs, we can amend the term sheet to add the exact T value and credit bands. For large committed pools we can tighten latency bands and increase the initial commit discount.

Julia — a couple of clarifications from the infra/ops side:

- GPU pool sizing: our token/sec number (T) is quoted per pool configuration (GPU type, NVLink, num GPUs). For a 4xA100-like pool we assume 1.0x base; for 8x pools you see ~1.85x tokens/sec (non-linear scaling due to KV-cache sharding). We should size for headroom (we recommend 20% headroom above your projected steady-state).
- Measurement windows: we provide server-side metrics aggregated at 1s granularity. For SLA computation we use the higher of (a) the customer’s measurement from their canary client and (b) Redwood’s server-side aggregated metrics — both must be within the SLA band to consider the window successful. This avoids noisy client-side sampling issues.
- Credits payout: credit is applied as % of monthly committed spend and appears on the following invoice; we add a one-time operational credit for onboarding misses if the root cause is Redwood infra.

Attached is the throughput-acceptance-matrix.xlsx with bucket thresholds and example calculation for how we translate tokens/sec shortfall into credit.
